holidays.name: Throw Out Your Leftovers Day
holidays.description: The day after the big feast, the fridge is a tower of foil-wrapped mystery containers. This is your official permission slip to inspect, sniff, and say goodbye to the turkey, stuffing, and cranberry sauce that have outstayed their welcome.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the post-Thanksgiving fridge clean-out.
holidays.funFact: Food safety experts commonly recommend eating or tossing cooked leftovers within about 3 to 4 days, so this date is a handy deadline.

holidays.name: National Square Dance Day
holidays.description: Grab your partner and do-si-do! This day celebrates square dancing, the American folk dance in which four couples form a square and move to the rhythmic calls of a caller. Boots and swishy skirts are optional but encouraged.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance that honors square dancing, a tradition rooted in European folk dances brought to North America and shaped into its modern form over the centuries.
holidays.funFact: Square dancing is the official state dance of more than 30 U.S. states, and a caller's patter can guide dancers through hundreds of different moves.

holidays.name: Customer is Wrong Day
holidays.description: A cheeky counterpoint to the old saying that the customer is always right. It's a day for a little humor about retail and service life, when workers get to imagine saying what they really think.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It plays on the famous retail motto and arrives right after the busy Black Friday shopping rush.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'the customer is always right' is often credited to early department store pioneers such as Harry Gordon Selfridge and Marshall Field.
